chunks.title: Proptosis, orbital syndromes & imaging
chunks.tldr: Rigid walls → mass pushes eye forward. Axial proptosis = intraconal; non-axial = extraconal. Bilateral → systemic (thyroid). Pulsating: CCF, AV malformation, sphenoid wing dysplasia (NF1). Worse with Valsalva/head down: orbital varix. Intermittent: mucocele. Measure with Hertel. Pseudoproptosis: high myopia, buphthalmos, lid retraction, contralateral enophthalmos. Optic neuropathy shows first as RAPD + colour loss. SOF syndrome: III, IV, VI + V1. Orbital apex: + optic nerve. Cavernous sinus: III, IV, VI + V1/V2, vision spared. CT for bone/trauma; MRI for soft tissue (no metal FB), preferred in kids; FNA biopsy >75% diagnostic.

cards.q: Orbital apex syndrome vs superior orbital fissure syndrome?
cards.a: Both affect III, IV, VI and V1; apex syndrome also involves the optic nerve (vision loss).

cards.q: Proptosis that increases with Valsalva suggests?

chunks.title: Thyroid eye disease: features
chunks.tldr: Autoimmune: TSH-receptor antibodies activate orbital fibroblasts → GAGs swell muscles, adipogenesis, fibrosis. Can be hyper-, eu- or hypothyroid; smoking and radioiodine worsen; linked to myasthenia. Commonest cause of uni/bilateral proptosis in adults. Signs: upper lid retraction (Dalrymple), lid lag (von Graefe), lagophthalmos, exposure, SLK. Muscles: IR > MR > SR > LR ('I'M SLow'); tendons spared (fusiform on CT); upgaze diplopia, IOP rise on upgaze. Compressive optic neuropathy at a crowded apex — may occur without much proptosis; RAPD, colour, VA. Ptosis in TED → think coexistent MG. Severe in 5–10%.

cards.q: Most commonly enlarged muscle in thyroid eye disease?
Earliest signs of dysthyroid optic neuropathy?
cards.a: RAPD and reduced colour vision, before acuity drops.

chunks.title: Thyroid eye disease: management
chunks.tldr: Team with endocrinology; avoid hypothyroidism; stop smoking; RAI risk (~15% new/worse TED) reduced by oral steroid cover; avoid RAI in active smokers. Grade with CAS. Mild: lubricants, selenium (mild active). Moderate-severe active: IV methylprednisolone pulses (better than oral), rituximab, radiotherapy (not with diabetic retinopathy), (now teprotumumab). Emergencies — optic neuropathy or severe exposure: high-dose IV steroid → orbital decompression. Inactive and stable ≥6 months → rehabilitative surgery in order: decompression → strabismus (recess tight IR/MR) → lids.
chunks.hook: Fix the order: Bones, then Muscles, then Lids.

cards.q: Correct sequence of rehabilitative surgery in TED?
cards.a: Orbital decompression, then strabismus surgery, then eyelid surgery.

chunks.title: Non-specific orbital inflammation
chunks.tldr: Idiopathic, usually unilateral, rapid, painful: lid/conjunctival oedema, proptosis, diplopia. Children: often bilateral with uveitis, disc oedema, eosinophilia. Can target one structure: myositis (tendon involved, unlike TED), dacryoadenitis, apex, perineuritis; may spread to cavernous sinus (Tolosa-Hunt). DDx: TED, lymphoma, sarcoid, GPA, IgG4-related disease, infection. Rx: oral steroids (dramatic response); recurrent → steroid-sparing (MTX, cyclophosphamide, infliximab), ± radiotherapy; biopsy if atypical/non-responding.
chunks.hook: Painful + rapid + steroid-responsive = NSOI; slow + painless = think lymphoma.

cards.q: How does orbital myositis differ from TED muscle enlargement on CT?
cards.a: Myositis involves the tendon insertion; TED spares the tendon (fusiform belly enlargement).

chunks.title: Orbital vs preseptal cellulitis
chunks.tldr: Orbital (postseptal): commonest cause of proptosis in children; usually from ethmoid sinusitis. Bugs: S aureus (incl. MRSA), Strep anginosus/pneumoniae/pyogenes; Hib rare now; anaerobes in adults. Signs: fever, proptosis, chemosis, painful restricted movement, ± RAPD. Risks: optic nerve compression, cavernous sinus thrombosis, intracranial abscess. Rx: cultures + IV 3rd-gen cephalosporin + vancomycin (+ metronidazole/clindamycin for anaerobes); CT/MRI; ENT; nasal decongestants. Subperiosteal abscess: observe if <9 y, medial, small, vision fine; otherwise drain + FESS. Preseptal: lid only — no proptosis, normal motility; oral co-amoxiclav, watch closely.
points: Cavernous sinus thrombosis: bilateral signs, V dysfunction, sick patient.
chunks.hook: Can it move without pain, no proptosis? Preseptal. Otherwise — orbital, admit.

cards.q: Commonest source of orbital cellulitis in children?
cards.a: Ethmoid sinusitis spreading through the lamina papyracea.

cards.q: Signs separating orbital from preseptal cellulitis?
cards.a: Proptosis, chemosis, painful/restricted eye movements, reduced vision/RAPD.

chunks.title: Invasive fungal sinusitis (mucormycosis)
chunks.tldr: Immunocompromised: diabetic ketoacidosis → Mucorales (Rhizopus, Mucor) in 80%; neutropenia → Aspergillus in 80%. Angioinvasion → necrosis: periorbital oedema, ptosis, ophthalmoplegia, visual loss, proptosis, CNS decline. Black eschar on nasal mucosa/palate; smear shows broad non-septate (Mucor) or septate (Aspergillus) hyphae. Death in days without treatment. Rx: correct immune problem/acidosis, IV amphotericin B (± posaconazole/caspofungin), aggressive debridement, possibly local amphotericin or exenteration.
chunks.hook: DKA + black palate + frozen eye = mucor — emergency.

chunks.title: Dermoids, mucoceles, meningoceles & vascular lesions
chunks.tldr: Dermoid/epidermoid: choristoma at a suture — commonly lateral brow (frontozygomatic); deep ones superotemporal, adult; CT bony scalloping; excise intact (rupture → granulomatous inflammation). Mucocele: frontal/ethmoid → non-axial proptosis (down-out); sphenoid → optic neuropathy; ENT marsupialisation. Meningocele/encephalocele: superomedial, enlarges with Valsalva. Varix: intermittent proptosis on Valsalva/bending, bleeds; embolise. CCF: direct high-flow (trauma, ICA aneurysm) — pulsating proptosis, bruit, chemosis, corkscrew vessels, high IOP, ophthalmoplegia; indirect dural low-flow (elderly women, spontaneous) — red eye mistaken for conjunctivitis. Doppler shows arterialised SOV; catheter angiography gold standard; embolise.
chunks.hook: 'Conjunctivitis' that never goes, with corkscrew vessels and high IOP = dural CCF.

cards.q: Most common location of a periorbital dermoid cyst?

cards.a: Reversed, arterialised flow in a dilated superior ophthalmic vein.

chunks.title: Vascular & paediatric orbital tumours
chunks.tldr: Capillary (infantile) haemangioma: commonest benign orbital tumour in children; 90% by 6 months, grows year 1, involutes over years; strawberry (superficial) or blue (deep); risks amblyopia (occlusion, astigmatism), strabismus. Rx oral propranolol (monitor HR, BP, glucose), steroids, surgery if refractory. Cavernous 'haemangioma' (venous malformation): commonest benign adult orbital tumour, women, intraconal → axial proptosis, hyperopia, choroidal folds; excise. Lymphangioma: kids, swells with URTIs, chocolate cyst bleeds; sclerotherapy. Rhabdomyosarcoma: commonest primary orbital malignancy in children, <10 y, rapid, superonasal; biopsy, chemo + RT; survival >90%.
chunks.hook: Child with eye pushed down and out over weeks = rhabdomyosarcoma — biopsy now.

chunks.title: NF1, optic glioma, lacrimal gland & lymphoma
chunks.tldr: NF1 (17q, AD): plexiform neurofibroma ('bag of worms', S-shaped lid), Lisch nodules, café-au-lait, sphenoid wing dysplasia (pulsating proptosis), optic glioma in ~15%. Optic nerve glioma: 75% <10 y, 30% NF1; pilocytic astrocytoma; anterior ones indolent; observe vs chemo/RT. Lacrimal gland mass: 50% inflammatory/lymphoid, 50% epithelial (half malignant). Pleomorphic adenoma: painless, slow → excise whole, don't biopsy. Adenoid cystic carcinoma: pain (perineural), bone erosion, poor prognosis. Lymphoma (MALT): elderly, painless, salmon patch, moulds to globe without bone erosion; 50% systemic → staging; orbital → RT. Metastases: breast, lung, prostate, melanoma; kids neuroblastoma (periorbital ecchymosis).
points: LCH: lytic orbital roof lesion in a child; curettage/steroid.
chunks.hook: Painless lacrimal lump = take it out whole; painful lacrimal lump = adenoid cystic.

cards.q: Why shouldn't a suspected pleomorphic adenoma be biopsied?
cards.a: Capsule breach causes recurrence and malignant transformation — excise en bloc.
